title: Reverse Words in a String
statement:
You get a string `s` of words and spaces, where a word is a maximal run of characters that are not spaces. `s` may begin or end with spaces and may have several spaces between two words, but it contains at least one word.

Return a new string holding the words of `s` from last to first, with exactly one space between neighbouring words and no space at either end.
constraints: s contains only English letters (upper and lower case), digits and spaces ' '
s contains at least one word

tests.name: Test 3
input: Alice does not even like bob

notes:
## Intuition

The answer lists the words of `s` from the last one to the first, so it is natural to read `s` from the right. Two indices bracket each word: `end` stops on its last character and `start` runs left until it meets a space. Spaces never get copied; they only separate words, so extra or leading/trailing spaces disappear on their own. The quick alternative splits on spaces, drops empty pieces and reverses the list, which is the same idea in library calls.

## Approach

1. Start with an empty `words` list and `end` at the last index.
2. Move `end` left past any spaces. If it falls off the start, there are no more words.
3. Set `start = end` and move it left until it reaches a space or the start of `s`.
4. The word is `s.slice(start + 1, end + 1)`; append it to `words`.
5. Continue from `end = start`.
6. Join `words` with single spaces and return.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "the sky is blue"` (15 characters). `end = 14` is on the final `e`; `start` runs left to the space at 10, so `"blue"` (indices 11 to 14) is added. From `end = 10` the space is skipped to `end = 9`, and `start` stops at the space at 7: `"is"`. Next comes `"sky"` (indices 4 to 6, `start` stops at 3), then `"the"` (indices 0 to 2, `start` ends at -1). `end = -1` ends the loop, and joining gives `"blue is sky the"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each index is passed by `end` or `start` once, and the slices copy each character once.
- Space: O(n) for the words and the result.

## Pitfalls

- Splitting on a single space keeps empty strings between double spaces; skip runs of spaces (or drop empty pieces).
- Check `end >= 0` after skipping spaces, or a string that begins with spaces adds an empty word at the end of the list.
- Do not build the result with a trailing or leading space; joining the list avoids it.
- The characters inside each word keep their order; only the word order is reversed.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `words` | words found so far, from last to first |
| `end` | index of the last character of the current word |
| `start` | index just before the current word (a space or -1) |

narration.2: Collect the words here in the order they are found, which is last to first.
narration.3: Start reading from the right end of the string.
narration.5: Keep going until every character has been passed.
narration.6: Skip spaces; they only separate words and are never copied.
narration.9: Only spaces were left (leading spaces of s)...
narration.12: end is on the last character of a word; start begins there.
narration.13: Move start left until it hits a space or runs off the front.
narration.16: The word lies strictly between start and end + 1; add it.
narration.17: Continue to the left of this word.
narration.19: Put exactly one space between the words.
